sources.articleTitle: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC

headline: Barnier Warns Against UK Seeking Cherry Picked EU Trade Agreement
seoTitle: Barnier Warns UK On EU Market Access
metaDescription: Michel Barnier states the EU will not permit the UK to select preferred elements of the single market, rejecting an a la carte economic approach.
aiSummaryBullets: Michel Barnier indicated that the European Union remains opposed to any selective trade agreements for the United Kingdom.
The former Brexit negotiator emphasized that member states would likely reject attempts to participate in the single market on a partial basis.
The remarks serve as a response to potential British efforts to secure favorable economic terms without adhering to all existing EU market rules.
aiContextParagraph: The relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union continues to be defined by discussions regarding trade access and regulatory alignment. Following the formal departure of the UK from the bloc, various negotiations have centered on how the two entities interact economically. Michel Barnier, who served as the chief EU negotiator during the Brexit process, recently addressed concerns regarding potential British proposals for a more flexible trade arrangement. He stated that the European Union would not accept a situation where the UK chooses to participate in specific sectors of the single market while opting out of others. This 'a la carte' approach, according to Barnier, would be firmly rejected by remaining EU member states who maintain that full market access requires adherence to established institutional rules. The statement highlights persistent tensions regarding the structural boundaries of post-Brexit economic cooperation and the rigid nature of European market regulations.
